related_questions.question: What is the meaning of diastolic blood pressure?
related_questions.snippet: Systolic blood pressure is the first number. It measures the pressure your blood is pushing against your artery walls when the heart beats. Diastolic blood pressure is the second number. It measures the pressure your blood is pushing against your artery walls while the heart muscle rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: Diastolic blood pressure is the bottom number in a blood pressure reading, representing the pressure in the arteries when the heart muscle is between beats, specifically when the heart is relaxed and refilling with blood. It's the minimum pressure in the arteries during the cardiac cycle. In a typical blood pressure reading of 120/80 mmHg, the diastolic pressure is 80 mmHg.

list.title: Systole vs. Diastole:
list.snippet: The heart alternates between contracting (systole) and relaxing (diastole). During systole, the heart pumps blood out, creating the systolic pressure. During diastole, the heart rests and refills with blood, creating the diastolic pressure.

list.title: Measurement:
list.snippet: Diastolic pressure is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is the second number in a blood pressure reading.

list.title: Importance:
list.snippet: Both systolic and diastolic blood pressure readings are important for assessing overall cardiovascular health. High diastolic pressure can indicate that blood vessels are becoming stiff or that there's an issue with the heart's ability to relax and refill.
